overview: This bill, the Strategic Subsea Cables Act of 2026, aims to protect the undersea cables and pipelines that carry most international internet traffic and much of the world's energy. It requires the President to sanction, through asset freezes and visa bans, foreign people and vessels found responsible for sabotaging such infrastructure or helping to do so. It calls for more U.S. involvement in international groups on cable protection, a multinational fleet of cable repair ships, and at least 10 dedicated State Department staff for these issues. It also orders reports on Chinese and Russian undersea activities and an intelligence assessment of past cable and pipeline damage incidents, including the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions, and creates a White House-level committee of federal agencies to coordinate cable security, speed up permits, and share threat information with cable companies. As of February 10, 2026, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say damage to a few undersea cables could disrupt communications, finance, and energy worldwide, so better coordination, faster repairs, and penalties for sabotage are overdue.
against: Critics say the bill adds a new committee and many recurring reports, and that sanctions for sabotage depend on proving who damaged a cable, which is often hard to establish.
